Subject: Post-bill collection triggers & VAT split — net terms for pilot

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — the pilot starts next month and finance asked me to align on billing terms ahead of kickoff. A few asks from our side:

- Can Redwood support an initial Net45 for the pilot (30–60k/month run-rate) with a review to Net30 after two consecutive on-time invoice cycles?
- We'd like a provisional credit ceiling of £75,000 (GBP) while we ramp; can you confirm any minimum deposit or milestone holdback you require?
- Our UK entity will be handling VAT — would Redwood accept routing UK invoices to our UK billing entity (we can provide VAT registration and tax evidence), or do you prefer Redwood invoice and remit VAT?

I attached a short credit request form to expedite bank/reference checks (novacare-credit-request-form.pdf).

Goal is to get procurement comfortable so we can unblock PO issuance next week. Happy to jump on a quick call with Marcus/Marissa if helpful.

Best,
Emily

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the form. Looping in Marcus (finance) and Marissa (contracts/accounts) to validate internal guardrails. Quick responses to your bullets:

- Net terms: We can offer Net45 for the pilot period with a formal review after two successive invoice cycles. If payment performance is positive we can accelerate to Net30.
- Credit ceiling and holdback: We typically do a provisional credit cap and a small initial holdback for first invoices (10%) until banking/credit checks clear. For your requested £75k ceiling, we can provisionally approve £60k pending bank reference and registration docs; we can increase nominally once references are confirmed.
- VAT routing: Either option is workable; if NovaCare prefers to receive and remit UK VAT directly, we need the VAT registration and a confirmation of billing entity (attach tax evidence). Alternatively, Redwood can invoice the UK entity and handle VAT if that simplifies procurement.

I've attached our internal playbook for staged netterms and billing cadence to show typical flows (redwood-netterms-playbook.pdf). Proposed next steps: 1) Emily shares bank reference and VAT registration, 2) Marcus runs provisional credit schedule, 3) Marissa prepares the billing appendix and DocuSign stub for signature.

If agreeable, I'll produce a short mutual action plan and an invoicing cadence document for signature.

Regards,
Olga Petrov

Hi Emily / Olga — thanks, I pulled together a provisional schedule so we're all aligned. Key items from finance:

1) Credit corridor: initial provisional ceiling £60,000 GBP for the first 60 days, subject to bank reference and company registration. After 60 days (two invoice cycles) we'll reassess; on-time payments allow movement to the requested £75,000 ceiling.

2) Net terms cadence: Net45 to start, review at first two invoice clears; automatic reversion to Net30 based on payment performance (2/2 on-time).

3) Holdback: 10% holdback on the first two invoices only (applied as retainage on final invoice for the invoice period) — this reduces exposure while proofs complete.

4) Billing currency and FX: We will bill in GBP for UK entity invoices. Please confirm whether NovaCare will accept GBP invoices net of VAT or if Redwood should invoice gross and remit VAT. If you want Redwood to handle VAT, we need authority to invoice the UK subsidiary and specific remit instructions.

5) Required docs: bank reference (PDF), company registration number, VAT registration certificate (if you expect to self-remit VAT).

Attached is the provisional-credit-schedule.xlsx with sample runway and exposure lines. Once we receive the documents we'll issue a short billing appendix for signature and activate the provisional ceiling.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Finance Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@novacare.com>

Subject: Re: Post-bill collection triggers & VAT split — net terms for pilot

Thanks Marcus — attaching our banking reference and VAT docs now (novacare-banking-reference.pdf). A couple clarifications from our procurement team:

- NovaCare prefers to self-account for UK VAT. We will take invoices net of Redwood's VAT charge (i.e., provide your billing to our UK subsidiary). If Redwood needs to invoice gross temporarily to simplify systems, we can switch after the first month, but our preference is to avoid Redwood remitting VAT on our behalf.
- Automatic reminders: we prefer one automated email reminder at 14 days overdue and one at 30 days overdue before any credit action. Could Redwood mirror that cadence?
- Electronic invoicing: can you enable e-billing (PDF via supplier portal) to speed acceptance?

We can also route a quick PO and supplier onboarding link after the billing appendix is final.

Best,
Emily

Emily — thanks for the quick turnaround on documents and for confirming VAT routing preference. Finalizing next steps below so procurement can push the PO:

2) Net45 payment terms will apply initially; we will review after two consecutive on-time payments and can accelerate to Net30.
